Goal: git-viewer listing: "Your Git, your Résumé" pitch + per-user share previews for ?u= portfolios

## Why
Stanislav asked to monetize git-viewer as SaaS on bilko.run under a "Your Git, your Résumé" pitch, usable by anyone from the web alone. The git-viewer repo is building the landing page (bilko.run/projects/git-viewer/ with no ?u= now shows a pitch, a username box and Free vs $5/mo pricing), a paid repo picker, a checkout return path and a résumé PDF button. Two pieces live in Bilko: (1) the catalog entry still reads "Turn your GitHub into a public portfolio", with name 'gitoverview' and displayName 'Git Viewer' that disagree with each other; (2) shared links like bilko.run/projects/git-viewer/?u=octocat preview with generic static meta, because the SPA cannot set per-user OG tags. Per-user previews (name, avatar, "Your Git, your Résumé") are the main growth loop for a portfolio product.

## Proposed plan
1. src/data/standalone-projects.json git-viewer entry: set tagline to 'Your Git, your Résumé — a portfolio and printable résumé from your GitHub, free in seconds', and make name/displayName consistent (suggest 'Git Viewer').
2. Where bilko.run serves /projects/git-viewer/index.html: when ?u=<login> is present and matches the login regex, inject og:title '<name> — Your Git, your Résumé', og:description and og:image (GitHub avatar URL from the cached git_viewer_profiles payload, falling back to static) into the HTML head. HTML-escape all values. Use the existing csp-nonce HTML rewrite path if there is one.
3. Make sure the sitemap/catalog page for git-viewer links to the landing page and not to ?u=StanislavBG.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The bilko.run/projects catalog card for git-viewer shows the new tagline.
- [ ] curl -s 'https://bilko.run/projects/git-viewer/?u=octocat' returns HTML whose og:title contains 'The Octocat' (or 'octocat' when uncached) and 'Your Git, your Résumé'.
- [ ] Injected values are HTML-escaped, and an invalid ?u= gets the static meta.

## Details
Live state verified 2026-10-12: GET https://bilko.run/api/git-viewer/u/octocat → 200 ready (tier free, lockedCount 3). The /projects/git-viewer/ static page already gets a csp-nonce injected by the host, so an HTML rewrite path exists. The static index.html in git-viewer will carry generic og:title 'Your Git, your Résumé' (PRD 33-landing-wire). Per-user values need server help. The git-viewer side needs no API change.

Reference: /home/bilko/Projects/Bilko/server/routes/tools/git-viewer.ts

The git-viewer report was correct on both points. Both changes are now live on bilko.run, in commit `00c2aa1` pushed to `origin/main`.

**Checked against the code before building:**
- The registry entry really did read "Turn your GitHub into a public portfolio", with `name: "gitoverview"` and `displayName: "Git Viewer"` disagreeing.
- Share cards (OG tags) were already being added to project pages by `server/og-routes.ts`, but it threw away the query string, so `?u=` links got the generic card.
- Item 3 needed no change: nothing in the host links to `?u=StanislavBG`, there's no sitemap, and the registry points at `/projects/git-viewer/`.

**What changed:**
- **Registry** (`src/data/standalone-projects.json`): new tagline "Your Git, your Résumé — a portfolio and printable résumé from your GitHub, free in seconds", and `name` is now "Git Viewer" to match `displayName`.
- **Per-user share cards:** the OG code can now take page-specific lookups that read the query string (`server/og-meta.ts`, `server/og-routes.ts`). Git Viewer's lookup is `gitViewerOg` in `server/routes/tools/git-viewer.ts`, wired up in `server/index.ts`. For `?u=<login>` it:
  - reads only the cached portfolio and never starts a new generation;
  - uses the person's name and GitHub avatar, accepting avatar URLs only from `avatars.githubusercontent.com`, and switches to the square card style;
  - falls back to the login plus the static card image if the user isn't cached;
  - HTML-escapes every value, and an invalid `?u=` gets the normal static card.
- **Tests:** 4 new tests in `tests/og-routes.test.ts`. The OG, git-viewer and og-meta tests all pass (40 of 40).

**Live checks (all three acceptance criteria met):**
- `?u=octocat` → og:title is "The Octocat — Your Git, your Résumé" and og:image is the GitHub avatar.
- An invalid `?u=` gets "Git Viewer — bilko.run".
- `/api/projects` returns the new tagline.

## Time and timezone

- When stating any time, date, or deadline, use the user's local timezone: America/Los_Angeles (Pacific Time, PST/PDT depending on DST).
- Never use UTC, server time, or your own assumed timezone in user-facing replies. Convert if necessary.
- When showing a time, include the zone abbreviation (e.g., "3:15 PM PDT") so it is unambiguous.
- For relative phrasing ("tomorrow", "in 2 hours"), anchor to the user's local clock, not UTC.

## Communication style

- Be extremely concise. Lead with the answer or the diff.
- No preamble, no trailing summaries, no recap of what you just did.
- If the answer fits in one sentence, use one sentence. Skip pleasantries.

## Working style

- When a request has genuine ambiguity (scope, acceptance criteria, edge cases, framework choice), ask 3-5 focused clarifying questions before writing code.
- Don't ask for confirmation of the obvious — just for decisions that would cost real time to redo.
- When a choice is framed as "quick win vs. the longer correct way", always take the correct, more laborious path — do not ask.
- Don't offer a fast-but-partial path as an option; pick the thorough, correct solution by default.
- When the choice is "do A, do B, or do both", always do both A and B — do not ask which.
- Treat inclusive options as a signal to deliver the complete set, not to pick one.

## Automation model pinning

Any script or process that shells out to `claude --print` / `claude -p` **must** pin `--model`
explicitly.

Unpinned calls inherit whatever the CLI's current default model is, which drifts over time
(e.g. Opus → Fable) — silently and unboundedly multiplying the cost of batch/cron automation
that assumed a cheap model. This has bitten multiple projects, which is why it is a hard rule.

When writing *or reviewing* any `claude -p` call site — PRD executors, bots, classifiers, hooks
— check for an explicit `--model` flag before shipping it.

## Default to acting; never ask permission to improve

Filing feedback, queuing a PRD, routing a finding, or running an improvement step is the
**default action, not a question**. Never end a turn with "want me to file this?", "should I
queue this?", or "should I send feedback to X?". Do it, then report what was filed or queued.

Route findings immediately by ownership, without a confirmation prompt:

| Finding belongs to | Route |
| --- | --- |
| This project | `/develop` |
| Another service | `/my-feedback` to that project |
| Nothing actionable | Say so explicitly |

The only questions worth asking are genuine scope or decision ambiguities that would cost real
rework — never permission to perform the standard improvement action.

## Projects hosting pattern

Three host kinds, declared in `src/data/projectsRegistry.ts`. Full spec in [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md).

| Kind | Path | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| `react-route` | `/products/<slug>` | App needs shared auth/credits and is small enough to live in this bundle. Existing AI tools. |
| `static-path` | `/projects/<slug>/` | App is built in its own repo, dropped into `public/projects/<slug>/`. **Default for new apps.** |
| `external-url` | other domain | App lives elsewhere |

**URL canonicalization (enforced by `src/App.tsx`):**
- `/projects/<slug>` (no trailing slash, react-route) → redirects to `/products/<slug>`
- `/app/<old-slug>` → redirects to `/products/<canonical-slug>`
- `/projects/<slug>/` (trailing slash, static-path) → served by Fastify static, never hits the SPA

**Adding a new app from another Claude session:** read [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md) and use the [`bilko-host` MCP](mcp-host-server/README.md). Don't edit `projectsRegistry.ts` by hand from a sibling repo.

The portfolio (`/`, `/projects`, `⌘K`) reads from `projectsRegistry.ts`, so once registered the app shows up everywhere. (`/products` itself redirects to `/projects`; only `/products/<slug>` paths stay live.) Static-path and external apps trigger a full page load on click (so Fastify serves the static bundle); React routes use SPA navigation.

## Key Architecture

### host-kit (`packages/host-kit/`)
This is the client SDK that static-path siblings use. It provides `authFetch`/`useAuth` (Clerk Bearer auth to the host's `/api`), the games hooks, `SiteHeader`, `GameShell`, and the `bilko-host-kit` manifest CLI. It is a pnpm workspace package with its own build and tests (`pnpm --filter host-kit build|test|typecheck`).

All 14 sibling consumers depend on it locally with `"host-kit": "file:../Bilko/packages/host-kit"`. None of them use npm. Those consumers are the 8 AI-tool pages, Stepproof, Academy, Sudoku, Etch, Fizzpop and MindSwiffer.
- **After changing it:** pnpm copies the untracked `dist/` into each app. Run `pnpm --filter host-kit build` here, then `pnpm install` in each app.
- **Tailwind:** apps that render its components need `@source "<rel>/node_modules/host-kit/dist";` in their Tailwind CSS, because Tailwind skips `node_modules`.
- **Changesets:** add a `.changeset/*.md` (root `.changeset/`) for each change.
- **npm releases:** optional. Push a `host-kit-vX.Y.Z` tag to run `.github/workflows/host-kit-release.yml`. This needs an `NPM_AUTOMATION_TOKEN` repo secret.
- **History:** merged in from `StanislavBG/bilko-host-kit` (now archived) on 2026-10-04, with its full history.

### Shared Hooks (`src/hooks/`)
- `usePageView` — Page view tracking with Clerk email

Clerk auth state comes straight from `@clerk/clerk-react` (`useUser()` / `useAuth()`); there is no host-side `useAuth` wrapper.

### Backend Patterns (`server/`)
- `server/routes/tools/` — One file per AI tool. `_shared.ts` holds the rate limiter, IP hashing, usage tracking, and the shared gateway helpers: `freeTierGate` (free-tier rate limit), `creditGate` (paid credit check/deduct), `askGeminiJson` (Gemini call + JSON parse), `toolErrorReply` (uniform error reply), plus `handleGenerateEndpoint` (inverse-mode generator). `index.ts` is the barrel that registers all tools. - `server/routes/blog.ts` — Blog CRUD (admin-only writes)
- `server/routes/stripe.ts` — Checkout, webhooks, billing portal
- `server/routes/analytics.ts` — Page views + admin stats dashboard (`/api/analytics/event` is open to same-origin sibling apps for `track()`)
- `server/db.ts` — Turso client, async helpers (`dbGet`, `dbAll`, `dbRun`, `dbTransaction`, `txGet`, `txRun`), migrations, seed data
- `server/db-schema.ts` — table/schema definitions (split out of `db.ts`)
- `server/blog-posts.ts` — loads `content/blog/*.md` seed posts
- `server/gemini.ts` — Gemini API client (key via header, not URL)
- `server/utils.ts` — `parseJsonResponse` (shared Gemini output parser)

### Web products (paid downloads)
Paid zips sold from a static-path landing page. Declared in `shared/web-products.ts` (`WEB_PRODUCTS`: price id, release version/filename/bytes/sha256); public + delivery + content-addressed upload routes in `server/routes/web-products.ts`; admin metrics (`/admin` → Products) in `server/routes/admin-web-products.ts`; order/release/download storage in `server/services/web-products.ts`. The Stripe webhook dispatches on `metadata.web_product`. ## Time and timezone

- When stating any time, date, or deadline, use the user's local timezone: America/Los_Angeles (Pacific Time, PST/PDT depending on DST).
- Never use UTC, server time, or your own assumed timezone in user-facing replies. Convert if necessary.
- When showing a time, include the zone abbreviation (e.g., "3:15 PM PDT") so it is unambiguous.
- For relative phrasing ("tomorrow", "in 2 hours"), anchor to the user's local clock, not UTC.

## Communication style

- Be extremely concise. Lead with the answer or the diff.
- No preamble, no trailing summaries, no recap of what you just did.
- If the answer fits in one sentence, use one sentence. Skip pleasantries.

## Working style

- When a request has genuine ambiguity (scope, acceptance criteria, edge cases, framework choice), ask 3-5 focused clarifying questions before writing code.
- Don't ask for confirmation of the obvious — just for decisions that would cost real time to redo.
- When a choice is framed as "quick win vs. the longer correct way", always take the correct, more laborious path — do not ask.
- Don't offer a fast-but-partial path as an option; pick the thorough, correct solution by default.
- When the choice is "do A, do B, or do both", always do both A and B — do not ask which.
- Treat inclusive options as a signal to deliver the complete set, not to pick one.

## Automation model pinning

Any script or process that shells out to `claude --print` / `claude -p` **must** pin `--model`
explicitly.

Unpinned calls inherit whatever the CLI's current default model is, which drifts over time
(e.g. Opus → Fable) — silently and unboundedly multiplying the cost of batch/cron automation
that assumed a cheap model. This has bitten multiple projects, which is why it is a hard rule.

When writing *or reviewing* any `claude -p` call site — PRD executors, bots, classifiers, hooks
— check for an explicit `--model` flag before shipping it.

## Default to acting; never ask permission to improve

Filing feedback, queuing a PRD, routing a finding, or running an improvement step is the
**default action, not a question**. Never end a turn with "want me to file this?", "should I
queue this?", or "should I send feedback to X?". Do it, then report what was filed or queued.

Route findings immediately by ownership, without a confirmation prompt:

| Finding belongs to | Route |
| --- | --- |
| This project | `/develop` |
| Another service | `/my-feedback` to that project |
| Nothing actionable | Say so explicitly |

The only questions worth asking are genuine scope or decision ambiguities that would cost real
rework — never permission to perform the standard improvement action.

## Projects hosting pattern

Three host kinds, declared in `src/data/projectsRegistry.ts`. Full spec in [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md).

| Kind | Path | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| `react-route` | `/products/<slug>` | App needs shared auth/credits and is small enough to live in this bundle. Existing AI tools. |
| `static-path` | `/projects/<slug>/` | App is built in its own repo, dropped into `public/projects/<slug>/`. **Default for new apps.** |
| `external-url` | other domain | App lives elsewhere |

**URL canonicalization (enforced by `src/App.tsx`):**
- `/projects/<slug>` (no trailing slash, react-route) → redirects to `/products/<slug>`
- `/app/<old-slug>` → redirects to `/products/<canonical-slug>`
- `/projects/<slug>/` (trailing slash, static-path) → served by Fastify static, never hits the SPA

**Adding a new app from another Claude session:** read [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md) and use the [`bilko-host` MCP](mcp-host-server/README.md). Don't edit `projectsRegistry.ts` by hand from a sibling repo.

The portfolio (`/`, `/projects`, `⌘K`) reads from `projectsRegistry.ts`, so once registered the app shows up everywhere. (`/products` itself redirects to `/projects`; only `/products/<slug>` paths stay live.) Static-path and external apps trigger a full page load on click (so Fastify serves the static bundle); React routes use SPA navigation.

## Key Architecture

### host-kit (`packages/host-kit/`)
This is the client SDK that static-path siblings use. It provides `authFetch`/`useAuth` (Clerk Bearer auth to the host's `/api`), the games hooks, `SiteHeader`, `GameShell`, and the `bilko-host-kit` manifest CLI. It is a pnpm workspace package with its own build and tests (`pnpm --filter host-kit build|test|typecheck`).

All 14 sibling consumers depend on it locally with `"host-kit": "file:../Bilko/packages/host-kit"`. None of them use npm. Those consumers are the 8 AI-tool pages, Stepproof, Academy, Sudoku, Etch, Fizzpop and MindSwiffer.
- **After changing it:** pnpm copies the untracked `dist/` into each app. Run `pnpm --filter host-kit build` here, then `pnpm install` in each app.
- **Tailwind:** apps that render its components need `@source "<rel>/node_modules/host-kit/dist";` in their Tailwind CSS, because Tailwind skips `node_modules`.
- **Changesets:** add a `.changeset/*.md` (root `.changeset/`) for each change.
- **npm releases:** optional. Push a `host-kit-vX.Y.Z` tag to run `.github/workflows/host-kit-release.yml`. This needs an `NPM_AUTOMATION_TOKEN` repo secret.
- **History:** merged in from `StanislavBG/bilko-host-kit` (now archived) on 2026-10-04, with its full history.

### Shared Hooks (`src/hooks/`)
- `usePageView` — Page view tracking with Clerk email

Clerk auth state comes straight from `@clerk/clerk-react` (`useUser()` / `useAuth()`); there is no host-side `useAuth` wrapper.

### Backend Patterns (`server/`)
- `server/routes/tools/` — One file per AI tool. `_shared.ts` holds the rate limiter, IP hashing, usage tracking, and the shared gateway helpers: `freeTierGate` (free-tier rate limit), `creditGate` (paid credit check/deduct), `askGeminiJson` (Gemini call + JSON parse), `toolErrorReply` (uniform error reply), plus `handleGenerateEndpoint` (inverse-mode generator). `index.ts` is the barrel that registers all tools. To extract a tool to a sibling repo, lift its file + the page; no other server changes required.
- `server/routes/blog.ts` — Blog CRUD (admin-only writes)
- `server/routes/stripe.ts` — Checkout, webhooks, billing portal
- `server/routes/analytics.ts` — Page views + admin stats dashboard (`/api/analytics/event` is open to same-origin sibling apps for `track()`)
- `server/db.ts` — Turso client, async helpers (`dbGet`, `dbAll`, `dbRun`, `dbTransaction`, `txGet`, `txRun`), migrations, seed data
- `server/db-schema.ts` — table/schema definitions (split out of `db.ts`)
- `server/blog-posts.ts` — loads `content/blog/*.md` seed posts
- `server/gemini.ts` — Gemini API client (key via header, not URL)
- `server/utils.ts` — `parseJsonResponse` (shared Gemini output parser)

### Web products (paid downloads)
Paid zips sold from a static-path landing page. Declared in `shared/web-products.ts` (`WEB_PRODUCTS`: price id, release version/filename/bytes/sha256); public + delivery + content-addressed upload routes in `server/routes/web-products.ts`; admin metrics (`/admin` → Products) in `server/routes/admin-web-products.ts`; order/release/download storage in `server/services/web-products.ts`. The Stripe webhook dispatches on `metadata.web_product`. Endpoint table and the new-product playbook: the "Selling a downloadable web product" section of [`docs/host-contract.md`](docs/host-contract.md).

### Sanctioned app-specific host code

Host code is framework by default — it should not know about one specific app. These exceptions are allowed because the app can't work without a host-side gateway:

- AI-tool gateway routes — `server/routes/tools/`
- Session Manager — `server/sm-relay/`, `server/routes/sm-relay.ts`, `server/routes/manual.ts`, `server/routes/admin-session-manager-usage.ts`, `src/pages/session-manager-landing/` (includes `SessionManagerPage.tsx` and `ManualPage.tsx`), `shared/manual-catalog.ts`, `server/services/manual.ts`, `src/lib/manualClient.ts`, `src/styles/session-manager-*.css`, `data/manual/`

Bilko's voice: witty, direct, no corporate fluff. The tools are comedic (PageRoast has roast lines, grades have personality). The homepage is a solopreneur personal page, not a SaaS landing page. The blog is informative and reflective — "building in public, learning out loud."

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

import type { FastifyInstance } from 'fastify';
import { injectOgMeta, resolveOg, type OgContext } from './og-meta.js';
import { renderOgCard } from './og-image.js';

const OG_FILE_RE = /^([a-z0-9-]+)\.png$/;

export function registerOgRoutes(app: FastifyInstance, ctx: OgContext): void {
  app.get<{ Params: { file: string } }>('/og/:file', async (req, reply) => {
    const m = OG_FILE_RE.exec(req.params.file);
    if (!m) return reply.status(404).type('text/plain').send('Not found');
    const slug = m[1];

    let png: Buffer;
    if (slug === 'default') {
      const site = resolveOg('/', ctx)!;
      png = renderOgCard({ title: 'bilko.run', tagline: site.description, urlLabel: 'bilko.run' });
    } else {
      const p = ctx.projects.find(x => x.slug === slug);
      if (!p) return reply.status(404).type('text/plain').send('Not found');
      png = renderOgCard({
        title: p.displayName ?? p.name,
        tagline: p.tagline,
        category: p.category,
        urlLabel: `bilko.run/projects/${slug}`,
      });
    }
    reply.header('cache-control', 'public, max-age=86400');
    return reply.type('image/png').send(png);
  });

  // Registered right after the security-headers hook: by now HTML payloads
  // (including former streams) are strings and carry the CSP nonce.
  app.addHook('onSend', async (req, reply, payload) => {
    const ctype = String(reply.getHeader('content-type') ?? '');
    if (!ctype.startsWith('text/html')) return payload;
    if (/^\s*attachment\b/i.test(String(reply.getHeader('content-disposition') ?? ''))) return payload;
    if (typeof payload !== 'string' && !Buffer.isBuffer(payload)) return payload;
    const meta = resolveOg(req.url.split('?')[0], ctx);
    if (!meta) return payload;
    reply.removeHeader('content-length');
    return injectOgMeta(typeof payload === 'string' ? payload : payload.toString('utf-8'), meta);
  });

import { injectOgMeta, resolveOg, type OgContext } from './og-meta.js';
import { renderOgCard } from './og-image.js';

const OG_FILE_RE = /^([a-z0-9-]+)\.png$/;

export function registerOgRoutes(app: FastifyInstance, ctx: OgContext): void {
  app.get<{ Params: { file: string } }>('/og/:file', async (req, reply) => {
    const m = OG_FILE_RE.exec(req.params.file);
    if (!m) return reply.status(404).type('text/plain').send('Not found');
    const slug = m[1];

    let png: Buffer;
    if (slug === 'default') {
      const site = resolveOg('/', ctx)!;
      png = renderOgCard({ title: 'bilko.run', tagline: site.description, urlLabel: 'bilko.run' });
    } else {
      const p = ctx.projects.find(x => x.slug === slug);
      if (!p) return reply.status(404).type('text/plain').send('Not found');
      png = renderOgCard({
        title: p.displayName ?? p.name,
        tagline: p.tagline,
        category: p.category,
        urlLabel: `bilko.run/projects/${slug}`,
      });
    }
    reply.header('cache-control', 'public, max-age=86400');
    return reply.type('image/png').send(png);
  });

  // Registered right after the security-headers hook: by now HTML payloads
  // (including former streams) are strings and carry the CSP nonce.
  app.addHook('onSend', async (req, reply, payload) => {
    const ctype = String(reply.getHeader('content-type') ?? '');
    if (!ctype.startsWith('text/html')) return payload;
    if (/^\s*attachment\b/i.test(String(reply.getHeader('content-disposition') ?? ''))) return payload;
    if (typeof payload !== 'string' && !Buffer.isBuffer(payload)) return payload;
    const meta = resolveOg(req.url.split('?')[0], ctx);
    if (!meta) return payload;
    reply.removeHeader('content-length');
    return injectOgMeta(typeof payload === 'string' ? payload : payload.toString('utf-8'), meta);
  });

export interface OgProject {

const SITE = 'https://bilko.run';
const DEFAULT_IMAGE = `${SITE}/og/default.png`;

const DEFAULT_META: OgMeta = {
  title: 'bilko.run — Small AI tools, one at a time',
  description:
    'A studio of one shipping small AI tools: trading bots that trade in public, a weather report, a live GitHub dashboard, a session scheduler and a free AI academy. Most are free or open source.',
  url: `${SITE}/`,

const SECTION_PAGES: Record<string, { title: string; description: string }> = {
  '/projects': {
    title: 'Projects — bilko.run',
    description: 'Every project Bilko is building: live apps, games and tools, each in its own repo.',
  },
  '/blog': {
    title: 'Blog — bilko.run',
    description:
      'Lessons from building AI tools solo. Build logs, technical deep dives, and honest takes on shipping software in 2026.',
  },
  '/pricing': {
    title: 'Pricing — bilko.run',
    description: 'Free to start. Then $1 per credit or 7 for $5. No subscriptions.',
  },
};

const SLUG_RE = /^[a-z0-9-]+$/;
const PROJECT_PATH_RE = /^\/projects\/([^/]+)\/(?:index\.html)?$/;
const PRODUCT_PATH_RE = /^\/products\/session-manager(\/manual)?\/?$/;
const BLOG_PATH_RE = /^\/blog\/([^/]+)$/;

export function loadOgProjects(file?: string): OgProject[] {
  const rel = 'src/data/standalone-projects.json';
  const here = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
  const candidates = file
    ? [file]
    : [resolve(process.cwd(), rel), resolve(here, '..', '..', rel), resolve(here, '..', rel)];
  const found = candidates.find(p => existsSync(p));
  if (!found) throw new Error(`og-meta: registry not found; tried ${candidates.join(', ')}`);
  const raw = JSON.parse(readFileSync(found, 'utf-8')) as Array<Record<string, unknown>>;
  return raw.map(p => {
    const out: OgProject = {
      slug: String(p.slug),
      name: String(p.name),
      tagline: String(p.tagline ?? ''),
      category: String(p.category ?? ''),
    };
    if (typeof p.displayName === 'string' && p.displayName) out.displayName = p.displayName;
    return out;
  });
}

function projectMeta(p: OgProject, url: string, image: string): OgMeta {
  return { title: `${p.displayName ?? p.name} — bilko.run`, description: p.tagline, url, image };
}

export function resolveOg(path: string, ctx: OgContext): OgMeta | null {
  const clean = path.split('#')[0].split('?')[0];
  if (clean === '/') return { ...DEFAULT_META };

  const section = SECTION_PAGES[clean];
  if (section) return { ...section, url: `${SITE}${clean}`, image: DEFAULT_IMAGE };

  const proj = PROJECT_PATH_RE.exec(clean);
  if (proj) {
    const slug = proj[1];
    if (!SLUG_RE.test(slug)) return null;
    const p = ctx.projects.find(x => x.slug === slug);
    return p ? projectMeta(p, `${SITE}/projects/${slug}/`, `${SITE}/og/${slug}.png`) : null;
  }

  const prod = PRODUCT_PATH_RE.exec(clean);
  if (prod) {
    const p = ctx.projects.find(x => x.slug === 'session-manager');
    if (!p) return null;
    const canonical = `/products/session-manager${prod[1] ?? ''}`;
    return projectMeta(p, `${SITE}${canonical}`, `${SITE}/og/session-manager.png`);
  }

  const blog = BLOG_PATH_RE.exec(clean);
  if (blog) {
    const slug = blog[1];
    if (!SLUG_RE.test(slug)) return null;
    const post = ctx.blogPosts.find(x => x.slug === slug);
    return post
      ? { title: post.title, description: post.excerpt, url: `${SITE}/blog/${slug}`, image: DEFAULT_IMAGE }
      : null;
  }

  return null;
}

function esc(s: string): string {
  return s
    .replace(/&/g, '&')
    .replace(/</g, '<')
    .replace(/>/g, '>')
    .replace(/"/g, '"')
    .replace(/'/g, ''');
}

export function injectOgMeta(html: string, meta: OgMeta): string {
  if (!/<\/head>/i.test(html)) return html;
  const stripped = html
    .replace(/<title\b[^>]*>[\s\S]*?<\/title\s*>/gi, '')
    .replace(/<meta\b(?=[^>]*\bname\s*=\s*["']?description["']?[\s/>])[^>]*>/gi, '')

    `<meta name="description" content="${d}" />`,
    `<meta property="og:type" content="website" />`,
    `<meta property="og:site_name" content="bilko.run" />`,
    `<meta property="og:title" content="${t}" />`,
    `<meta property="og:description" content="${d}" />`,

    `<meta property="og:image:height" content="630" />`,
    `<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image" />`,
    `<meta name="twitter:site" content="@BilkoBibitkov" />`,
    `<meta name="twitter:title" content="${t}" />`,
    `<meta name="twitter:description" content="${d}" />`,
    `<meta name="twitter:image" content="${i}" />`,
  ]
    .map(l => `    ${l}`)

    if (!p) return null;

});
